When SpaceX isn't launching rockets unmanned, it turns out it's busy acquiring AI companies. This February, the company behind Starlink quietly acquired xAI, which also owns Twitter, now renamed to X. In April, SpaceX struck a deal with Cursor, a competitor to Claude Code and OpenAI Codex. As of August 14, the acquisition has been completed. The company, now renamed SpaceXAI, has also recently launched the Grok Bot and Grok 4.6 model with Cursor's assistance.

Updated August 14, 2026: SpaceXAI has completed its acquisition of Cursor.

Updated June 16, 2026: SpaceX acquired Cursor one week after going public.

Below is the original report with updates:

SpaceX strikes $10 billion deal with Cursor ahead of $60 billion acquisition

Cursor has long been popular among software engineers who use Macs to write AI programs, and was one of the first services to connect large language model AI to the application development process.

In April, the two companies stated that SpaceX and Cursor were "working closely together with the goal of building the world's best AI for coding and knowledge work."

The initial collaboration agreement included SpaceX paying Cursor $1 billion:

Cursor, in April, before this acquisition, further disclosed details of the collaboration:

Cursor is working with SpaceX to accelerate our model training efforts. Composer is the first agentic coding model we've rolled out in six months. After that, Composer 1.5 will scale up reinforcement learning by more than 20x. Composer 2 further adds continued pretraining to achieve frontier-level performance at a fraction of the cost of other models. Every increase in compute translates into significant gains in model capability. We've always wanted to push our training efforts further, but we've been constrained by compute. Through this partnership, our team will leverage xAI's Colossus infrastructure to significantly enhance the intelligence of our models.

The collaboration between SpaceX and Cursor strengthens the competitive position of a rival to Anthropic's Claude Code and OpenAI Codex agentic coding software.
